主要内容: On November 27, 2018, Under Secretary David Malpass testified before the U.S. Senate Foreign Relations Subcommittee, discussing U.S. and global growth, international economic policy, and the role of multilateral institutions. He highlighted progress in the U.S. but noted challenges abroad, particularly in international economic policy. Malpass outlined major policy developments in 2018, including efforts to improve transparency in international debt, engagement with China on its One Belt, One Road (OBOR) initiative, and the enhancement of U.S. national security through the Foreign Investment Risk Review Modernization Act (FIRRMA). He also mentioned the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) and the America Crece initiative to promote growth in the Western Hemisphere. The testimony emphasized the importance of currency stability, transparency, and accountability in international financial institutions. Malpass addressed the U.S. Senate Foreign Relations Subcommittee on Multilateral International Development on November 27, 2018. He emphasized the importance of trade, investment, and finance transactions driven by private capital to achieve faster economic growth and security with partners. Malpass highlighted the refocusing of the Financial Stability Board (FSB) on systemic risk, including an activities-based approach for insurance activities, the wind-down of non-stability work streams, and the evaluation of existing policies before developing new ones. He also noted the appointment of Randy Quarles as the FSB’s next Chair, the first American to hold the role. Malpass discussed the World Bank’s commitment to reforms, including sustainability in lending, enforcement of graduation policies, and differential pricing. He also addressed the challenges posed by the 'Troika of Tyranny'—Venezuela, Cuba, and Nicaragua—and the impact of their actions on neighboring countries. The U.S. is working to implement FIRRMA, enhance debt transparency, and challenge China’s unfair trade practices. As Brexit approaches, the Treasury is analyzing risks to the international financial system and working with the EU and UK to ensure continued market access for U.S. firms.

股票实体.名称: Foreign Investment Risk Review Modernization Act (FIRRMA)
